contentBlocks.text: How to Appeal a SASSA Grant After Initial Decline

A declined grant application is not the end of the road. You have 90 days to file an appeal with the Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA). This guide covers every step from receiving your decline notification to receiving the tribunal ruling.
This guide is for SASSA applicants who received a decline notification and need step-by-step instructions on how to file an appeal.

steps.title: Read your decline notification
steps.description: Read your SASSA decline notification carefully to understand the specific reason.

steps.title: Gather your evidence
steps.description: Gather evidence that directly refutes the decline reason (UIF letter, bank statements, NSFAS letter).

steps.title: Visit the appeal portal
steps.description: Visit the ITSAA appeal portal at srd.dsd.gov.za (for SRD) or your local SASSA office (for other grants).

steps.title: Verify your identity
steps.description: Enter your ID number and phone number to verify your identity via OTP.

steps.title: Select months and upload evidence
steps.description: Select the month(s) you are appealing and provide your supporting evidence.

steps.title: Save your reference number
steps.description: Submit and save your Appeal Reference Number for tracking.

steps.title: Monitor for updates
steps.description: Monitor the portal for updates and wait for the tribunal ruling.

contentBlocks.title: 90-Day Deadline
contentBlocks.text: You have 90 days from the date of the decline notification to file your appeal. The tribunal has 60-90 days to issue a ruling.

faqs.question: What if it has been more than 90 days since my decline?
faqs.answer: Unfortunately, appeals cannot be accepted after 90 days. You must submit a completely new grant application.

faqs.question: Can I appeal in person at a SASSA office?
faqs.answer: Yes. For non-SRD grants, you can visit your nearest SASSA office with your documents and request a manual appeal submission.
